{{short description|Circle tangent to two sides of a triangle and its circumcircle}}

In [[plane geometry]], a '''mixtilinear incircle''' of a [[triangle]] is a [[circle]] which is [[tangent]] to two of its sides and internally tangent to its [[Circumscribed circle|circumcircle]]. The mixtilinear incircle of a triangle tangent to the two sides containing [[Vertex (geometry)|vertex]] <math>A</math> is called the ''<math>A</math>-mixtilinear incircle.'' Every triangle has three unique mixtilinear incircles, one corresponding to each vertex.
[[File:Define of Mixtilinear cirlce.jpg|thumb|350x350px|<math>A</math>-Mixtilinear incircle of triangle <math>ABC</math>]]

== Proof of existence and uniqueness ==

The <math>A</math>-[[excircle]] of triangle <math>ABC</math> is unique. Let <math>\Phi</math> be a transformation defined by the [[Function composition|composition]] of an [[Inversive geometry|inversion]] centered at <math>A</math> with radius <math>\sqrt{AB \cdot AC}</math> and a [[Reflection symmetry|reflection]] with respect to the angle bisector on <math>A</math>. Since inversion and reflection are [[Bijection|bijective]] and preserve touching points, then <math>\Phi</math> does as well. Then, the image of the <math>A</math>-[[excircle]] under <math>\Phi</math> is a circle internally tangent to sides <math>AB, AC</math> and the circumcircle of <math>ABC</math>, that is, the <math>A</math>-mixtilinear incircle. Therefore, the <math>A</math>-mixtilinear incircle exists and is unique, and a similar argument can prove the same for the mixtilinear incircles corresponding to <math>B</math> and <math>C</math>.<ref name=":1" />

== Construction ==
[[File:Mixtilinear circle.jpg|thumb|400x400px|The hexagon <math>XCABYT_A</math> and the intersections <math>D, I, E</math> of its 3 pairs of opposite sides.]]
The <math>A</math>-mixtilinear incircle can be constructed with the following sequence of steps.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|title=Mixtilinear Incircles|url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/MixtilinearIncircles.html|access-date=2021-10-31|website=mathworld.wolfram.com|language=en}}</ref> 
# Draw the [[incenter]] <math>I</math> by intersecting angle bisectors.
# Draw a line through <math>I</math> perpendicular to the line <math>AI</math>, touching lines <math>AB</math> and <math>AC</math> at points <math>D</math> and <math>E</math> respectively. These are the tangent points of the mixtilinear circle.
# Draw perpendiculars to <math>AB</math> and <math>AC</math> through points <math>D</math> and <math>E</math> respectively and intersect them in <math>O_A</math>. <math>O_A</math> is the center of the circle, so a circle with center <math>O_A</math> and radius  <math>O_AE</math> is the mixtilinear incircle

This construction is possible because of the following fact: 

=== Verrier's lemma ===
The incenter is the midpoint of the touching points of the mixtilinear incircle with the two sides.

=== Proof ===
Let <math>\Gamma</math> be the circumcircle of triangle <math>ABC</math> and <math>T_A</math> be the tangency point of the <math>A</math>-mixtilinear incircle <math>\Omega_A</math> and <math>\Gamma</math>. Let <math>X \neq T_A</math> be the intersection of line <math>T_AD</math> with <math>\Gamma</math> and <math>Y \neq T_A</math> be the intersection of line <math>T_AE</math> with <math>\Gamma</math>. [[Homothety]] with center on <math>T_A</math> between <math>\Omega_A</math> and <math>\Gamma</math> implies that <math>X, Y </math> are the midpoints of <math>\Gamma  </math> arcs <math>AB </math> and <math>AC </math> respectively. The [[inscribed angle]] theorem implies that <math>X, I, C </math> and <math>Y, I, B </math>  are triples of collinear points. [[Pascal's theorem]] on hexagon <math>XCABYT_A </math> inscribed in <math>\Gamma </math> implies that <math>D, I, E </math> are collinear. Since the angles <math>\angle{DAI} </math> and <math>\angle{IAE} </math> are equal, it follows that <math>I </math> is the midpoint of segment <math>DE </math>.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Baca|first=Jafet|title=On Mixtilinear Incircles|url=https://www.awesomemath.org/wp-pdf-files/math-reflections/mr-2020-02/mr_2_2020_mixtilinear.pdf|access-date=October 27, 2021}}</ref> 
== Other properties ==

=== Radius ===
The following formula relates the radius <math>r</math> of the incircle and the radius <math>\rho_A</math> of the <math>A</math>-mixtilinear incircle of a triangle <math>ABC</math>:<math display="block">r = \rho_A \cdot \cos^2{\frac{\alpha}{2}}</math>


where <math>\alpha</math> is the magnitude of the angle at <math>A</math>.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Yui|first=Paul |date=April 23, 2018|title=Mixtilinear Incircles |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/00029890.1999.12005146|access-date=October 27, 2021 | journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=106|issue=10| pages=952–955 | doi=10.1080/00029890.1999.12005146|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Relationship with points on the circumcircle ===

* The midpoint of the [[Arc (geometric)|arc]] <math>BC</math> that contains point <math>A</math> is on the line <math>T_AI</math>.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|last=Chen|first=Evan|author-link=Evan Chen |title=Euclidean Geometry in Mathematical Olympiads|publisher=MAA|year=2016| isbn=978-1-61444-411-4| location=United States of America|pages=68}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web| last=Nguyen| first=Khoa Lu|date=2006 |title=On Mixtilinear Incircles and Excircles |url=https://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2006volume6/FG200601.pdf|access-date=November 27, 2021}}</ref>
* The quadrilateral <math>T_AXAY</math> is [[Projective harmonic conjugate|harmonic]], which means that <math>T_AA</math> is a [[symmedian]] on triangle <math>XT_AY</math>.<ref name=":1" />

=== Circles related to the tangency point with the circumcircle ===

<math>T_ABDI</math> and <math>T_ACEI</math> are [[Cyclic quadrilateral|cyclic quadrilaterals]].<ref name=":2" />

=== Spiral similarities ===

<math>T_A</math> is the center of a spiral similarity that maps <math>B, I</math> to <math>I, C</math> respectively.<ref name=":1" />

== Relationship between the three mixtilinear incircles ==

=== Lines joining vertices and mixtilinear tangency points ===
The three lines joining a vertex to the point of contact of the circumcircle with the corresponding mixtilinear incircle meet at the external center of [[Homothety|similitude]] of the incircle and circumcircle.<ref name=":0" /> The [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers|Online Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]] lists this point as X(56).<ref>{{Cite web|title=ENCYCLOPEDIA OF TRIANGLE CENTERS|url=https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/etc.html|access-date=2021-10-31|website=faculty.evansville.edu}}</ref> It is defined by [[trilinear coordinates]]: 
<math display="block">\frac{a}{b+c-a} : \frac{b}{c+a-b} : \frac{c}{a+b-c},</math> 
and [[Barycentric coordinate system|barycentric coordinates]]: 
<math display=block>\frac{a^2}{b+c-a} : \frac{b^2}{c+a-b} : \frac{c^2}{a+b-c}.</math>

=== Radical center ===
The radical center of the three mixtilinear incircles is the point <math>J</math> which divides <math>OI</math> in the ratio: <math display="block">OJ:JI=2R:-r</math>where <math>I, r, O, R</math> are the incenter, inradius, circumcenter and circumradius respectively.<ref name=":3" />
